units.name: Atlas

tier.basis: The registry gives this series no tech tiers: its tech eras are periods of history, not gates a player unlocks.

cost_band.basis: The registry treats the series as having no unit prices. The tabletop's C-bill price and Battle Value exist, but the research ranks 'Mechs by weight class instead.

mobility.notes: Speed from the BattleTechWiki's tabletop figures for the AS7-D, top speed against the Centurion CN9-A reference: a little slower than that medium 'Mech, with a slow cruising pace that lets most enemy 'Mechs outrun it. The registry names no standard tank, so the reference medium 'Mech is the comparison. MechWarrior Online's stock AS7-D, with its standard engine, is slower still, and the game gives it its heaviest movement profile. It has no jump jets. Handling stays pivot, the two-legs default: nothing in the sources shows it unable to turn in place. Its torso twists only partway, which the mount proposal reflects.

body.notes: A two-legged assault 'Mech with a torso, arms and working hands, at the top of the assault weight class, topped by the skull-shaped 'Death's Head' cockpit. Size large because the size examples put assault mechs there. Its tabletop quirks include Battlefists (its hands are tuned for punching, a small to-hit bonus) and Distracting (its look worsens enemy morale checks under the optional morale rules); both only change numbers. The roomy head holds a folding satellite dish for long-range communications.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class order decided: the registry's armour map puts assault 'Mechs at heavy. Few 'Mechs carry more protection: its armour weighs almost as much as a whole light 'Mech, and it is thickest on the chest front and the legs. Zonal: armour and structure are split by location as on every 'Mech, so a destroyed right torso takes the autocannon and the right arm with it. Directional: the rear torso plating is much thinner than the front, roughly a third as thick on the centre torso. The AS7-D has no CASE, so an ammunition explosion is not contained (the later AS7-K added it). In MechWarrior Online the wiki credits its standard engine with letting it take very heavy damage and still fire its centre-torso lasers.

sensors.notes: The registry gives no sight distances for this series, so the band is the medium proposal. The AS7-D carries only the standard sensors every 'Mech has: no ECM, active probe or TAG. Its tabletop Improved Communications quirk lets it shrug off the weakest level of enemy ECM interference; that only changes numbers.

armament.name: Autocannon/20 (Defiance 'Mech Hunter)
armament.summary: The signature gun, in the right torso, meant for close fighting. In MechWarrior Online one shot from it can cripple a lighter 'Mech, and that game's Inner Sphere autocannons fire a single heavy shell each time rather than a burst. The BattleTechWiki adds that this gun lacks a cooling jacket and tends to run hot, and that it has only a small stock of rounds. The cited pages say nothing about how the shell travels, so projectile is the family default.

armament.name: LRM 20 (FarFire Maxi-Rack)
armament.summary: The long-range weapon, in the left torso. In MechWarrior Online the missiles home on a locked target, and they can be fired indirectly at enemies the Atlas cannot see while a teammate keeps the lock or holds TAG on the target. Inside a minimum distance they do almost nothing, and an enemy carrying ECM blocks the lock unless the Atlas is just outside that minimum or a teammate helps. In the tabletop design the launcher sends its twenty missiles in waves of five, fires directly or indirectly, and carries enough reloads for twelve full salvos; big salvos eat ammunition fast. MechWarrior Online's heat scaling covers this launcher, though the stock Atlas has only one.

armament.name: SRM 6 (TharHes Maxi)
armament.summary: A rack of six short-range missiles in the left torso, next to the long-range launcher, that backs up the autocannon in close fights with its own stock of reloads. No cited page says its missiles steer, so it is coded as unguided rockets.

armament.name: Medium lasers (four Defiance B3M)
armament.summary: One laser in each arm and a pair in the centre torso. In the tabletop design the centre-torso pair faces backwards to discourage enemies circling behind it; MechWarrior Online's AS7-D treats that pair as guns it can still return fire with after heavy damage. They need no ammunition, only heat. Beam is the laser family default, as the cited pages do not describe the shot.

crew.notes: One MechWarrior pilots it from the skull-shaped cockpit; players drive it in MechWarrior Online. Its tabletop Command 'Mech quirk gives its side a small initiative bonus, which only changes numbers; the AS7-D-DC variant, not this model, trades the rear lasers and a ton of missile reloads for a command console, and some Lyran refits add a dual cockpit. It is not an OmniMech, so battle armour can ride it only with magnetic clamps; no seats are recorded for that.

on_death.notes: None of the cited pages describes what happens when an Atlas is destroyed. Players drive it in MechWarrior Online, where a downed pilot goes back to choose a 'Mech again, so it is respawn under the rule for piloted games. Its unprotected ammunition can explode inside it when hit.

strengths.why: Few 'Mechs are as heavily protected: its armour alone weighs nearly as much as a light 'Mech, so it soaks enormous punishment and keeps fighting.
The huge autocannon can cripple a lighter 'Mech with one hit.
The LRM 20 lets it fight at long range too, including indirect fire at targets teammates lock or mark.
Its standard engine lets it absorb very heavy damage spread over its locations, and the centre-torso lasers still answer back.
Hands plus sheer mass make it a frightening brawler hand to hand; tales tell of it picking up medium 'Mechs and hurling them.

weaknesses.why: Its pace is its one real flaw: most enemy 'Mechs can outrun it, so it struggles to catch anything that chooses to leave.
Enemies aim for the right torso, where knocking out one location takes the autocannon and the attached right arm.
The autocannon, short-range missiles and lasers all need it to close in, which its slowness makes hard.
Its LRMs do almost nothing against enemies that get close.
The autocannon, LRMs and SRMs all feed from a fixed stock, and large salvos use it up quickly.

countered_by.why: Faster 'Mechs choose the fight: running away is their best chance against it, and flankers go for its thin back, which only two rear-facing lasers cover.
An enemy with an always-on ECM denies its LRMs a lock unless it closes in or a teammate breaks the jamming.

counters.why: Light and medium 'Mechs crumble: one autocannon hit can cripple them, and on paper one Atlas could destroy a whole battalion of Stingers with little armour lost, if they cannot escape.
The BattleTechWiki's own example: a battalion of these light 'Mechs could fall to one Atlas while barely scratching it.

combos.why: A teammate holding TAG on a target keeps the lock for its LRMs, even through ECM, so it can hit enemies it cannot see.
A teammate whose PPC shots keep an enemy ECM switched off lets its LRMs lock on again.

units.memorable: The skull-faced giant designed so that its look alone would scare enemies: a walking fortress whose autocannon can cripple a lighter 'Mech in one hit.
units.as_player: A slow, towering brawler. You walk in behind a wall of armour, twist the torso to bring the huge autocannon onto a target, and finish fights with missiles and lasers up close, while your LRMs arc onto anything a teammate locks or marks. Watch heat and ammunition, turn your shoulder to spread damage, and guard your right side, where the big gun lives. Fast enemies can run from you or slip behind you.

uncertain.note: Rests on the BattleTechWiki's Autocannon∕20 page (read, not cited for lack of room): its tabletop long range is well under the reference autocannon's, so short. The Atlas page also calls it the close-range weapon.
Rests on the BattleTechWiki's SRM 6 page (read, not cited for lack of room): same tabletop long range as the autocannon/20, so short.
Rests on the BattleTechWiki's Medium laser page (read, not cited for lack of room): same tabletop long range as the autocannon/20, so short, although that page calls the laser a midrange weapon.

Off-screen because the cited pages say it fires indirectly on targets that teammates lock or mark. By reach alone, the BattleTechWiki's LRM 20 page (read, not cited) gives a tabletop long range a little under one and a half times the reference's, which would be medium.

Cannon because MechWarrior Online fires one heavy shell per shot; the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Weapons page (read, not cited) says Inner Sphere autocannons fire a single shell, while the BattleTechWiki's Autocannon∕20 page says guns of this class fire singly or in bursts depending on the model.
Lists only what the cited pages show it locking onto (enemy 'Mechs). The tabletop launcher can attack any target, and the pages do not say whether MechWarrior Online's can be fired without a lock.
The tabletop centre-torso lasers face backwards; MechWarrior Online's AS7-D appears to mount them facing forward. The entry keeps the tabletop design as the registry's design source.

Directional rests on the MegaMek record for the AS7-D (github.com/MegaMek/mm-data, read, not cited for lack of room), which gives the front and rear torso armour; the cited BattleTechWiki page says only that the chest front is especially thick.
Naval targets are listed because the tabletop game has naval vessels (the BattleTechWiki's Combat Vehicle page, read, not cited); none of the cited pages mentions ships.
The Master Unit List refused the request (HTTP 403), so no official role line was read. The MegaMek record gives the role Juggernaut, which names none of our roles either way.
No cited page shows the Atlas's death; respawn follows the rule for 'Mechs players drive in a game where they come back.
The MechWarrior Online Wiki pages were last edited in 2014 and were not checked against later patch notes; MechWarrior 5: Clans was not checked for the Atlas at all.

fit_notes.wanted: lock-on that can also arc over cover onto targets a teammate locks (indirect fire)
fit_notes.note: The LRM locks on, but it can also fire indirectly, like a lobbed shot, at enemies only teammates see. The delivery order makes it lock-on, so the siege role's coding rule (a lobbed weapon that reaches long or further) does not pick it up, though the MechWarrior Online Wiki calls it long-range bombardment.

atypical.note: The autocannon/20 is a Ballistic weapon, which the damage map turns into kinetic; it fires one heavy shell at a time in MechWarrior Online, so it is a cannon, and our cannon family allows only armour-piercing or explosive damage.
